findings.statement: The F14 caller wave was rendered by .github/scripts/generate-caller.py through converge-caller.yml, NOT by Repository.Policy.Caller.Render. The Swift renderer exists and carries F3 fixture parity, but it has never been the live producer: `git grep render-caller -- .github/workflows` returns nothing, while converge-caller.yml calls the Python generator at lines 289 and 321 and its 922nd run completed 2026-08-05T12:21:19Z. Any statement that the fleet's callers came from the Swift owner is unsupported at this head.

generate-caller.py's `parse` mode has no Swift counterpart. Repository Policy CLI exposes render-caller with --form current|direct only. Until Repository.Policy.Caller.Parse exists, the incumbent is load-bearing for the preserve-existing-inputs fail-closed path.

71 of 104 files are RETAINED-NO-OWNER. Almost all are .github/scripts/validate-*.py and audit-*.py — linter and validator predicates whose intended owners are swift-linter (Swift syntax and AST semantics) and Workspace validators (checkout and package-graph facts), per the standing ownership split. NEITHER owner is realised for these predicates. F16 as scoped in PROGRAMME.md cannot retire them from inside this repository; they are cross-repository work in swift-linter and Workspace. This is the dominant term in STOP-F16-PURITY and it should be filed as exact-owner issues on those repositories.

swift-institute/Skills carries NO root Package.swift at this head (measured; positive control: swift-primitives/swift-percent-primitives returns the file, swift-institute/.github returns 404). #394 comment 5205766701 states Skills carries a root manifest and was caught by the dry run at 67 lines → 25. Both cannot be true of the same head. PR-D therefore evaluates the manifest term FIRST, so Skills reports .noManifest — the reason it is actually out — while the bespoke exception entry remains as a guard should it ever gain a manifest.

PR-B needs no manual cache-key recut. The universal workflow's bootstrap key derives from `git rev-parse HEAD:Tools/InstituteCI` (swift-ci.yml lines 501 and 2556) — the tree OID of that ONE directory, whose spelling is already annex-correct. Any content change inside it recuts the key automatically, and no other Tools path participates in a cache key (unfiltered `git grep HEAD:Tools` returns exactly those two lines). The same-commit coupling the brief required is satisfied vacuously; a hand-written key bump would have been the hazard, not the fix.
